item.title: OpenTelemetri
item.author: emecas
item.description:
OpenTelemetry
https://opentelemetry.io/
The open standard for telemetry

OpenTelemetry (OTel) is a leading open-source framework designed to help developers monitor and understand the performance of complex, cloud-native applications. It was created by merging two major projects, **OpenTracing** and **OpenCensus**, under the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF).

Here is a breakdown of why it’s a big deal in the software world:

### Core Benefits

* **Vendor Neutrality:** You can instrument your code once and send your data to any backend (like Prometheus, Jaeger, or commercial tools). This prevents “vendor lock-in,” allowing you to switch providers without rewriting your application code.
* **Unified Signals:** It brings together **Traces** (the journey of a request), **Metrics** (performance data over time), and **Logs** (timestamped events) into a single, correlated view.
* **Broad Support:** It offers native SDKs for over 12 programming languages and features more than 900 integrations.

item.title: Apache Shenyu
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Apache Shenyu
Java native API Gateway for service proxy, protocol conversion and API governance.
https://shenyu.apache.org/

https://github.com/apache/shenyu

Feature List

- Language: provides .NET, Python, Go, Java client for API register
- Proxy: Support for Apache® Dubbo™, Spring Cloud, gRPC, Motan, SOFA, TARS, WebSocket, MQTT
- Security: Sign, OAuth 2.0, JSON Web Tokens, WAF plugin
- API governance: Request, response, parameter mapping, Hystrix, RateLimiter plugin
- Observability: Tracing, metrics, logging plugin
- Extensions: Plugin hot-swapping, dynamic loading
- Dashboard: Dynamic traffic control, visual backend for user menu permissions
- Cluster: NGINX, Docker, Kubernetes

item.title: zipkin
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Zipkin
https://zipkin.io/

Zipkin is a distributed tracing system. It helps gather timing data needed to troubleshoot latency problems in service architectures. Features include both the collection and lookup of this data.

If you have a trace ID in a log file, you can jump directly to it. Otherwise, you can query based on attributes such as service, operation name, tags and duration. Some interesting data will be summarized for you, such as the percentage of time spent in a service, and whether or not operations failed.
